title: Modeling and Simulation of the Rotax 912 ULS Aircraft Engine Using GT-SUITE
content: The development of high-fidelity simulation models has become an essential component in the design, optimization, and performance evaluation of modern aircraft propulsion systems. In this study, a comprehensive one-dimensional thermodynamic model of the Rotax 912 ULS aircraft engine was developed using the GT-SUITE simulation platform. The model incorporates the major engine subsystems, including the fuel tank, fuel pump, carburetor, intake and exhaust manifolds, cylinders, and exhaust system, enabling a detailed representation of the engine's air-path and fuel delivery processes under operating conditions. The developed model was employed to predict the engine performance characteristics, with particular emphasis on brake power and torque. Simulation results were validated against the manufacturer's experimental performance data, demonstrating excellent agreement with deviations of less than 2% for both power and torque across the investigated operating range. The close correlation confirms the reliability and predictive capability of the proposed simulation model. The findings indicate that GT-SUITE provides an effective framework for accurately reproducing the thermodynamic behavior of piston aircraft engines and offers significant potential for future investigations involving engine calibration, performance optimization, fuel consumption analysis, emission prediction, and the evaluation of alternative aviation fuels without the need for extensive experimental testing.
